title: Concentration terms
examples: What is the difference between molarity and molality?
When should I use mole fraction instead of mass percentage?
Can I calculate ppm if I only have grams and liters?

explain.say: Today we look at how to measure concentration in solutions.

items: Concentration tells us how much stuff is dissolved.
Different units measure different things about the solution.
We will learn four common ways to express this.

explain.say: First we learn about mass percent, which is grams in grams.
Next we look at parts per million, which is for very small amounts.
Mole fraction compares moles of one substance to total moles.

draw.text: Mole Fraction = moles component / total moles

explain.say: Finally molality uses moles of solute over kilograms of solvent.
In real life, knowing concentration helps us make strong enough solutions.

faq.q: What is the main difference between molarity and molality?
faq.a: Molarity uses liters of solution, while molality uses kilograms of solvent. This difference matters when temperature changes.
asks: Does temperature affect molarity more than molality?
Why is molality better for temperature changes?

faq.q: When should I use mass percent versus ppm?
faq.a: Use mass percent for relatively large amounts, like in a lab beaker. Use ppm when the amount is tiny, like in environmental samples.

faq.q: Can I use mole fraction if I don't know the total volume?
faq.a: Yes, mole fraction only depends on the moles of the components present. You only need the moles of each substance.
asks: Do I need volume for mole fraction?
What if I mix two gases?

faq.q: Is molality always calculated using the solvent's mass?
faq.a: Yes, molality specifically requires the mass of the solvent, not the total mass of the solution. This is a key distinction to remember.
asks: Does 'solution' mean solvent or total mass?
If I use total mass, am I calculating molality?

faq.q: Are these concentration units related to the state of matter?
faq.a: Molarity and molality are for solutions. Mole fraction can apply to gases or liquids. Mass percent and ppm are general mass ratios.
asks: Can I use these for gases?
What if the solute is a gas?

facts: Mass percent is calculated as (mass of solute / mass of solution) times one hundred.
Parts per million (ppm) is useful for measuring very low concentrations of substances.
Mole fraction is a ratio of moles of one component to the total moles of all components.
Molality is defined as moles of solute dissolved per kilogram of solvent.

quiz.say: A solution contains 15 grams of salt in a total solution mass of 100 grams. What is the mass percent concentration?
quiz.why: Mass percent is simply the mass of the solute divided by the total mass of the solution, multiplied by one hundred.

wrong.0: This mistake happens if you forget to divide by one hundred when calculating the percentage.
wrong.1: This is a ratio, but the question asks for the percentage value, which requires multiplying by one hundred.
wrong.2: This gives the decimal ratio, but the required answer format is the percentage value.

quiz.say: If you dissolve 0 point 001 grams of pollutant in 1 kilogram of water, what is the concentration in ppm?
quiz.why: To find ppm, you multiply the mass ratio by one million. 0 point 001 times one million equals one.

wrong.0: This mistake forgets to multiply by one million, keeping the concentration too low.
wrong.1: This happens if you multiply by one thousand instead of one million.
wrong.2: This incorrectly divides the final value, suggesting the concentration is even smaller.

quiz.say: A solution is made from 2 moles of potassium chloride and 1 mole of water (assuming water is the solvent). What is the mole fraction of potassium chloride?
quiz.why: Mole fraction is the moles of the component divided by the total moles of everything mixed together. Two over three is correct.

wrong.0: This is actually correct, but if the student writes the fraction incorrectly as '2/3', it might be marked wrong if the system expects the full calculation.
wrong.1: This incorrectly compares the moles of solute only to the moles of solvent, ignoring the total.
wrong.3: This mistake forgets to add the moles of the solvent to the total moles.
